public_rationale: Marcus said the industry “seemed” increasingly reliant on circular financing. Scoring that as a firm assertion that circular arrangements accounted for a growing share of financing would strengthen his words and impose an unstated measure. Deal disclosures could make his impression understandable, but they would not provide a decisive test of the claim as written. The rules allow plain-reading scoring for firm claims; that approach does not apply here.
limitations: This classification does not assess whether particular circular financing arrangements existed or increased.
The accompanying statement about a meme is not separately graded.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI industry has appeared to rely increasingly on circular financing.

statement.excerpt: The industry seemed to increasingly rely on circular financing, so much so that an alternative NSFW framing of circular financing became a meme.
statement.document_title: Sam Altman and the day Nvidia’s meteoric rise came to an end

from_speaker: The industry seemed to increasingly rely on circular financing
an alternative NSFW framing of circular financing became a meme
our_interpretation: “Seemed” qualifies the assertion as an impression of increasing reliance. It does not commit the speaker to a measured increase in circular financing.
Requiring an increasing share of industry financing would add a measure and a firm commitment that the speaker did not supply.
The meme reference illustrates the perceived prominence of circular financing. Establishing that a meme existed would not settle the screened proposition about increasing reliance.
criteria.support_condition: No decisive support condition can be specified for the qualified impression without strengthening it into a different claim. Disclosed reciprocal investments and purchases could provide grounds for that impression.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No decisive contradiction condition can be specified for the qualified impression. A stable or declining measured share would test an added quantitative proposition.
